KEY MESSAGE 1...High pressure along the Eastern Seaboard moves 
out to sea as a cold front approaches from the west.

High pressure along the Eastern Seaboard moves out to sea 
this morning while a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley 
continues to track east. With the high offshore, southerly flow
develops and increases on Thursday. A warm and humid day, at 
least by mid-September standards, sets up on Thursday with highs
in the low to mid 80s and surface dew points in the mid to 
upper 60s. Some showers, perhaps a thunderstorm, may move into 
the southern Poconos, Lehigh Valley, and far northwest New 
Jersey starting around midday and into the late afternoon.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Scattered showers and a few storms are possible
Thursday night as a cold front moves through the region. 

The aforementioned cold front will track from northwest to 
southeast across the region Thursday night, clearing the region 
by Friday morning. As it does so, isolated to scattered showers 
and perhaps a few storms will be possible across most of the 
area. However, shower and storm activity associated with this 
front will be outrunning instability as it tracks into the area,
with a nocturnal inversion developing and only modest elevated 
instability remaining. Some locally heavy rainfall can't be 
entirely ruled out given PWATs of 1.5 to 2 inches, but coverage 
looks limited and the front looks progressive enough that hydro 
concerns are not anticipated. Severe weather is not anticipated.

The front will usher in a drier airmass for Friday, but 
temperatures will only cool by a couple of degrees relative to 
Thursday. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...A stretch of unsettled weather will begin 
Saturday night into Sunday, continuing into the first half of 
next week. Monitoring the potential for heavy rain.

As we head into the weekend, mid-level ridging that has been 
centered over portions of the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic will 
slowly begin to retrograde southwestward towards the Gulf Coast.
Enhanced northwesterly flow aloft will then overspread the 
region beginning this weekend as multiple disturbances pass to 
the north over portions of Ontario and Quebec. At the surface, 
high pressure centered north of the region will shift eastward 
and offshore Saturday as a low pressure system tracks out of the
Ohio Valley and Great Lakes region towards the area. An 
associated warm front looks to move through the area Sunday 
morning, with a cold front passing through the area by Monday. 
At this time, this front looks likely to stall just south of the
region through the middle of next week. 

Saturday should be a dry and seasonable day with temperatures 
generally topping out in the 70s to near 80. Beginning Saturday 
night, chances for showers and storms will begin to increase 
across the area as the low pressure and associated frontal 
boundaries begin their approach to the region. Sunday into 
Sunday night, scattered to numerous showers and storms are 
expected across the region. It currently appears that 
instability will be modest at best limiting any severe threat. 
However, PWATs look to be near 2 inches with deeply saturated 
vertical columns. Given this, at least a limited hydro threat 
could evolve. Currently, WPC has placed far northwestern 
portions of our eastern PA counties in a Marginal Risk (1 of 4) 
Excessive Rainfall Outlook for Saturday night, with that risk 
expanding across the entire area Sunday. 

Once the front clears the region Sunday night or Monday, 
uncertainty increases substantially. Guidance agrees that the 
frontal boundary will stall to the south of the region with a 
few waves of low pressure riding along it. Should the boundary 
stall just south of the region or even over southern parts of 
the area, scattered shower and storm chances will likely 
continue through mid-week. If it stalls farther south, it may 
not be quite as unsettled across our region. For now, most of 
the region has PoPs ranging from 30-50% Monday through 
Wednesday. 

Higher confidence exists in near or slightly below normal 
temperatures across the region for the early parts of next week 
north of the front.
